transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Lately I can’t seem to focus on my work the way I used to—my mind keeps drifting to everything that could go wrong, and I have to reread the same documents over and over. As a real estate broker, I'm just so terrified I'm going to miss something critical in a contract and ruin my reputation.
Did these worries start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or have they been ongoing even without one? Also, about how long have they been happening?

These worries have been wearing me down for a little over a year now. They really started when a few major life changes hit all at once—my youngest niece left for college, my ex-husband remarried, and I began seriously thinking about retirement while dealing with a very volatile housing market.

Do you find yourself worrying about many different things even when those life changes or market stressors are not actively happening, or are your symptoms mainly tied to those specific stressors? Have the worries continued at the same level even after any of those situations settled down?

Yes, the worries are constant and not tied to just one thing; my mind constantly chains them together, spiraling from a work issue to my mortgage, health insurance, and eventually fearing I'll end up old and alone. I also worry endlessly about my niece at college, and this has been going on continuously for over a year now without ever really settling down, even when I try to tell myself to stop.

Along with the constant worrying, have you also had symptoms like feeling restless or on edge, getting tired easily, muscle tension, irritability, trouble sleeping, or your mind going blank? Which of these have been happening most days?

Almost daily, I lie awake until 1 or 2 AM and wake up exhausted by 4 or 5, while my shoulders and neck constantly feel like concrete from tension. I also find my mind going completely blank mid-sentence during client meetings, which is incredibly embarrassing. It has left me feeling so constantly on edge and exhausted that I've even started turning down social plans.
